identity.description: Sherlock (sherlock-project/sherlock) is an open-source Python command-line OSINT tool that hunts down social media accounts by username across 400+ social networks. It is not a hosted SaaS app and has no official vendor API.
identity.identity_notes: Confirmed as the Sherlock Project's GitHub CLI tool (MIT, pipx/pip/Docker/dnf install). Many unrelated 'Sherlock' products exist (Sherlock Domains MCP by Fewsats, dotnet-sherlock-mcp, Sherlock data room, etc.), and many third-party Apify actors wrap Sherlock. None of those are the vendor product.

auth.scopes_notes: No API exists, so there are no auth scopes. Sherlock does not require API keys or login for the sites it checks.

access.production_restrictions: No vendor credentials are issued. Install the open-source CLI locally (pipx, pip, uv, Docker, or dnf) and run it; no account or API key is needed.

read_ops: search for a username across 400+ social networks
api.limitations: No official hosted API; the project is primarily a CLI. Bellingcat's toolkit page says there is no official Sherlock API. Only a PyPI package (sherlock-project) and a Python notifier hook were seen in search snippets, not verified on official pages.

open_questions: Check github.com/sherlock-project directly for any official MCP server or API; searches found none published by that org, so mcp.official is left unknown.
Confirm whether the PyPI package sherlock-project exposes a documented Python API (QueryNotify notifier class was seen only in a search snippet, not on an official page).
Rate limits and webhooks do not apply because no hosted API was found; confirm there is no hosted endpoint on the official docs.

Apify-hosted wrappers (e.g. ntriqpro/sherlock-username-osint, blackfalcondata/sherlock-username-osint-scraper) are third-party and require an Apify token; they were not verified beyond search snippets.
Breadth is rated Limited on the basis that Sherlock is a single-purpose read-only username search; it is not a SaaS app with a resource model.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented CLI/library interface.
API surface is limited; toolkit would cover few actions.
